snapshot_copy.implementation: fingerprint before and after in the live tree; does not copy STATUS, sidecar, or referenced receipts into a private snapshot
snapshot_copy.contract: requires an immutable private copy and verifier execution against that copy
snapshot_copy.impact: A file can change after the first hash and before or during the scan, then change back before the final hash; that transient can be missed. A peer can also mutate the bytes the scan is reading. The before/after check detects many races, but it is not a snapshot boundary.

normalized_hashes.implementation: fingerprint uses raw shasum first 16 hex for STATUS, sidecar, and receipts
normalized_hashes.contract: requires per-file raw SHA-256 plus normalized receipt hash where the existing convention defines one
normalized_hashes.impact: The implementation detects all raw byte changes, including harmless terminal-newline changes, but does not expose the normalized digest pair required by the contract. It can produce transient instability for a formatting-only mutation and cannot prove the normalized identity used by STATUS.

bounded_reexec.implementation: JEV_TRANSIENT_ATTEMPT defaults to 1; first change execs with JEV_TRANSIENT_ATTEMPT=2; attempt >=2 returns rc10 without reexec
bounded_reexec.what_is_proven: The child environment receives attempt=2 through env, so a normal first run has at most one recapture and two scans.
bounded_reexec.remaining_gap: A caller can start with JEV_TRANSIENT_ATTEMPT=2 or a nonnumeric value and bypass the first-attempt semantics; nonnumeric comparison behavior is not an explicit fail-closed usage path. It does not create an unbounded loop, but the script should reject externally supplied attempts outside {1,2} or reserve the variable as internal-only.

exit_10.evidence: Repository search found exit 10 only in the transient specification/rule and lane-status implementation. Existing lane-status codes occupy 2-9; foundation stage aggregation treats any nonzero as RED but does not assign code 10 itself.
exit_10.bound: Foundation/gates.sh would collapse rc10 to stage RED if lane-status were ever wired; the structured lane-status output must carry TRANSIENT_UNSTABLE so callers do not misread aggregate RED as durable failure.

sidecar_path.contract_risk: verify-other-reasons.sh supports JEV_SIDECAR, but lane-status's fingerprint does not. A JEV_SIDECAR fixture or alternate sidecar can be scanned/verified without its actual input being fingerprinted; the canonical sidecar can change instead and cause unrelated instability.
sidecar_path.repair: Use the same JEV_SIDECAR default/path resolution as the verifier, and include the resolved path in the fingerprint manifest.

clause_matrix.revision_hash_pair: PARTIAL: HEAD plus raw path hashes, no normalized pair and no copied-input manifest
clause_matrix.bounded_retry: MOSTLY_PASS: two normal attempts, external counter validation incomplete
clause_matrix.transient_exit: PASS: rc10 and no-verdict text exist, subject to caller preserving the distinction

ruling: The implementation is a useful bounded before/after race detector, not a faithful implementation of the full Q92 snapshot contract. It must not be used to claim immutable snapshot verification or promoted sidecar safety until private-copy execution, normalized hashes, input-path configuration, and attempt validation land.
no_claim: No claim that the observed ARM B/C behavior proves private snapshot semantics, no claim that exit 10 is consumed distinctly by foundation, and no claim that alternate JEV_SIDECAR inputs are protected.
